Archstone Security · Research · FedRAMP

FedRAMP 20x agency adoption, by the numbers.

FedRAMP has issued 33 20x authorizations in the 461 days since the first, on Jul 25, 2025. 3 of them have an agency authorization from anyone other than the FedRAMP PMO, which records one on every 20x listing. Of the 13 held by GRC and compliance-automation vendors, zero have an agency customer.

Those figures understate the program. GRC and compliance-automation vendors are heavily over-represented: they hold 13 of the 33 20x authorizations (39%). By the category providers choose for their own listings, GRC tools are 6% of 20x authorizations against 3% of traditional FedRAMP authorizations issued over the same period. None of those 13 has an agency customer. Agencies do buy GRC tools — all 8 GRC products authorized the traditional way have an agency behind them — just not through 20x, where the wave of GRC listings tracks vendors selling 20x readiness more than agency demand. Set the GRC vendors aside and 3 of the remaining 20 have an agency (15%), not 9%. The adoption 20x does have is AI platforms: ChatGPT Enterprise and API Platform, Gemini for Government and Perplexity Enterprise and API Platform. It is narrow: three agencies, one of them on all three. Even at 15%, 20x remains far from the traditional path, where every agency-path authorization starts with a sponsor.

Data FedRAMP Marketplace, Oct 29, 2026 Records 778 Last checked Oct 29, 2026 Download the 20x rows (CSV)

20x changes where in the process certification is granted but doesn't shorten the adoption timeline.

Every row starts on the day the product's marketplace listing entered the process. The grey bar runs to its 20x authorization; the dashed line runs from there to today. The shaded band is where a traditional FedRAMP authorization usually lands, middle half of products, measured the same way from the listing date. A traditional agency-path authorization comes with its sponsoring agency, so it is the point where an agency is relying on the product. For 20x that point has not arrived.

In processIn process, pilotAuthorizedSince authorization, no agency ATOHas an agency ATOListing re-certifiedTraditional, middle half of products

3 authorized 20x products are left out because their status history starts at authorization. Agency ATO dates are not in the export, so a filled tail means an agency relies on the product now, not since the date it was authorized. Pilots are included here because the question is how long agency adoption takes, which the invitation did not shorten. Both tracks are timed from the marketplace listing; preparation before a listing appears is not visible on either.

In the 20x pipeline now

9320x products in process
0with an agency named

Products in Initial Implementation or In Process on the 20x track. A traditional agency-path authorization needs a sponsoring agency before it starts; a 20x one does not, and so far none in the queue has one. The count may be low. Another 14 listings are in the same Initial Implementation intake status but carry the marketplace's traditional-track label, with no sponsoring agency. One of them describes its own trust center as a FedRAMP 20x trust center, and the same provider also has a separate 20x listing, so the marketplace's track label for listings in intake is not reliable.

Not counted as removals (24)

These listings are missing from the current export but are not counted as removals. Superseded (11): the provider holds a FedRAMP Certified listing under the same marketplace ID with a suffix added, which is how the marketplace records an uplift or re-authorization; the older listing was never updated. Brief appearance (13): the listing was not in the export when tracking began and was gone again within 14 days. Most are "In Process" records whose last recorded update is years old. The export does not say why a listing appears or is withdrawn, and this page does not infer either; open a row's history for the evidence.

The obvious objections, answered from the same data

"It's too new" and "20x is mostly Low" are the two replies this gets. Both are checked below against traditional FedRAMP authorizations issued in the same window. Traditional agency-path authorizations start with a sponsor by design, so the traditional share is close to 100% by construction; the comparison that matters is how far 20x sits from it after the same amount of time.

How these numbers are made

  • Source. The FedRAMP Marketplace's own JSON export, downloaded on a schedule and kept as dated snapshots. The page is rebuilt whenever the export changes.
  • Agency ATO means an agency other than the FedRAMP PMO listed on the product. The PMO records an agency use on every 20x authorization, so the marketplace's own authorization count shows at least one for every 20x product. That entry is removed everywhere on this page.
  • Authorization date is the marketplace's certification date for the product. The export lists the agencies on each product but not the date each agency signed, so this measures reliance as it stands today, not when it happened.
  • Traditional FedRAMP is the agency and JAB authorization track. The marketplace export, and the CSV download on this page, label it "Rev5".
  • Assessors are the 3PAO each provider names on its listing, matched to FedRAMP's directory of recognized assessors (kept in this site's repository, updated Oct 15, 2026), with the spelling variants providers use mapped to one name. For listings still in process the named assessor is the provider's own statement.
  • GRC and compliance vendors are identified from a separately maintained provider classification feed (data as of Oct 16, 2026), matched by provider name, and shown alongside the GRC business category providers choose for their own marketplace listings.
  • AI platforms are identified from a short provider list maintained alongside the GRC feed and applied to 20x products only. The marketplace's own "Artificial Intelligence (AI)" category is not used here: several AI products, including ChatGPT and Gemini, are not tagged with it.
  • Reclassification. No 20x record in the current export carries status history from before 2025 or an agency ATO inherited from a traditional authorization. Products authorized on both tracks are noted under the objections table; their agencies count toward traditional FedRAMP. A listing that is only FedRAMP Ready on one track is not counted as a match, since Ready is not an authorization. Snapshots are kept so that a record converted in place will show up when two exports are compared.
  • Track labels for new listings. Listings in the Initial Implementation intake status carry a traditional or 20x track label that does not always match the program the provider is pursuing, and at least one provider is listed twice, once on each track. Authorized products and agency ATOs are not affected; counts of products still in process should be read as approximate.
  • Limits. Withdrawn and expired products are not in the export. Class A 20x entries without an authorization date are included in totals and left out of anything plotted by date.
